title: Service ranking depends on the harness regime
caption: Every dot is one paired JVM comparison; horizontal jitter separates repeats. Red outlines retain recorded warnings. No percentiles are pooled. JMH changes caller/sampling/iteration/reset/consumption and uses eight one-second measurement iterations, versus a contiguous 30 seconds for the custom recorder; this is not an isolated timer intervention.

title: The small-value service advantage changes with cache policy
caption: Two paired repetitions per configuration. The three contrasts within a block share the same Chronicle anchor and are dependent. Unbounded Caffeine changes capacity policy, metadata and layout; it does not replace the bounded main comparison or isolate heap placement. Red outlines show retained warnings.

title: The baseline response reversal persists with equal trace-array geometry
caption: Each treatment has two fresh paired forks, 4 KiB values, zero ballast, 50,000 intended arrivals/s and 60/4/30-second phases. In the right panel both patterns retain identical long/boolean array lengths, with 10 Caffeine/9 Chronicle max humongous regions. Updated keys are 1,939 versus 25,532. The logical pattern still changes active read keys, ordering and lifetime together. Red outlines show any warning in the pair; both uniform-control pairs and one repeated-control pair are warning-free.

title: GC wall time and operation-tail probability use different denominators
caption: All displayed forks remain separate: three anchor pairs and single high-pressure discovery pairs. GC intersects few timed calls even when it consumes substantial wall time. The right panel counts service intervals intersecting GC intervals of at least 1 ms; it is not a count of independent stalls or proof that each whole call exceeds every shown latency threshold. At 336 MiB, all large-pause overlap in one Caffeine fork lies in 312 of 28,508,698 calls (0.0010944%), while GC occupies 39.36% wall time.

title: Matched-arrival service and response answer different questions
caption: Two paired forks per payload/pressure, same long trace and 50,000 intended arrivals/s. Every phase completes its intended operations, with matched paired write counts. These are paced service durations, not saturated-service replacements. Response favors Chronicle already at baseline in this workload. All JIT, host and dropped-demand warnings remain visible as red outlines.

title: The 8 KiB pilot did not justify a larger campaign
caption: One discovery pair per point with a ten-second measurement, 12/2-second preparation and 32,768 residents. Chronicle/Caffeine service p99.9 ratios are 1.1047 and 1.1711; pressure does not improve the ratio. The predeclared worth rule stops after four workload JVMs, with no confirmation or post hoc switch to a rarer primary endpoint. Red outlines retain endogenous dropped-churn warnings.

title: A full service tail reveals what a single percentile omits
caption: One 4 KiB/336 MiB discovery pair, not a confirmed crossover threshold. Full retained positive-survival bins are plotted without smoothing or pooling; the terminal zero cannot be drawn on the log axis. Caffeine p99.9/p99.99 are 8.367/19.887 µs, while p99.999 reaches 35.783 ms; Chronicle p99.999 is 1.465 ms. Finite sample resolution and correlated stall episodes constrain inference; zero observations do not establish zero risk.
